This position leads the implementation of academic program, curriculum, degree requirement, policy, and faculty governance actions across School of Nursing programs. The role serves as an advanced subject matter resource on academic program implementation and governance-related processes, helping ensure that decisions are properly routed, documented, communicated, and carried through to systems, catalogs, program materials, workflows, and accreditation records.
45% - Academic Program Alignment & Policy Liaison

The incumbent exercises a high degree of judgment and autonomy in interpreting requirements, resolving complex implementation issues, identifying risks and downstream impacts, and advising faculty, staff, program leaders, and campus partners on appropriate pathways and actions. The position develops implementation strategies, timelines, documentation practices, and communication plans; leads complex academic program improvement projects; and advances consistent, transparent, and effective academic operations across programs.  #CA-DS
30% - Faculty Governance & Academic Operations Support
15% - Academic Program Continuous Improvement Project Management
10% - Team Participation & Cross-Functional Support

Strong technical proficiency with office, documentation, and reporting tools to develop high-quality tracking systems, reports, materials, and records that support academic program operations and decision-making.
Demonstrated commitment to advancing diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging and to supporting equitable and transparent academic and administrative processes.

Advanced knowledge of academic policies, regulatory requirements, and institutional approval processes related to health professions education, including faculty governance, accreditation, Registrar, Graduate Studies, and other campus review functions, with the ability to apply this knowledge to complex academic program operations across multiple programs.
General knowledge of the academic mission of the School of Nursing.

Advanced knowledge of health professions education program administration, curriculum requirements, and operational processes, with the ability to serve as a subject matter resource on implementation of program changes, policy requirements, and governance-related actions.

Advanced analytical and operational planning skills to assess complex issues, identify risks and dependencies, evaluate downstream impacts, and develop effective solutions that improve program quality, consistency, and operational effectiveness.
Demonstrated ability to develop, implement, and improve complex processes and systems supporting academic program operations, documentation, compliance, and cross-program coordination.

Advanced project management skills to lead multiple high-complexity initiatives simultaneously, develop project plans, establish timelines and deliverables, monitor progress, manage risk, and guide projects from planning through completion.

Strong strategic communication skills, including the ability to prepare clear written materials, communicate complex policy and procedural requirements, facilitate stakeholder understanding, and tailor communications to faculty, leadership, campus partners, and administrative audiences.

Advanced interpersonal, consultation, and collaboration skills to build effective working relationships across academic and administrative units, coordinate with multiple stakeholders, and influence implementation of program actions and process improvements.

Demonstrated ability to exercise a high degree of independent judgment and autonomy in managing work of broad scope and complexity, resolving issues without clear precedent, and making sound recommendations related to program operations, governance processes, and implementation strategy.

Advanced organizational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to manage complex records, track multiple concurrent workstreams, maintain audit- and accreditation-ready documentation, and ensure accurate follow-through on governance and program implementation activities.

Advanced knowledge of data management, documentation methods, and reporting practices sufficient to monitor implementation progress, evaluate operational impacts, identify issues, and communicate findings and recommendations to leadership and stakeholders.

Demonstrated ability to lead process improvement and standardization efforts across programs or functional areas, including development of tools, workflows, documentation standards, and implementation practices that increase efficiency and consistency.

Demonstrated ability to function as a lead resource or technical expert in a specialized area, including providing guidance to peers, supporting continuity of operations through cross-training, and promoting consistent implementation practices across programs.

Demonstrated ability to handle sensitive and confidential information with discretion and sound judgment and to apply institutional expectations related to privacy, documentation, and data stewardship.
